prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has taken and passed the first-year courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Applied knowledge of business organization.

Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering for the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to manage the activities subject to the engineering projects described in competence CG01.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to solve problems.
Ability to make decisions.
Ability to consider environmental factors in decision-making.
Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team.
Attitude of motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.
Ability to organize and plan.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to interpret technical documentation.
Ability to work in a team.

Students should be able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their area of study.
Students should have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.

Be able to acquire basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems in environmentally friendly business settings, including manufacturing systems and processes, industrial quality, metrology, and planning.

syllabus_topics: Block 1. Manufacturing Systems 1.1. Systems, Processes and Manufacturing Technologies. 1.2. Introduction to Planning and Analysis of Manufacturing Systems. 1.3. Automated Manufacturing.

Block 2. Technologies and Material Removal Forming Processes. 2.1. Introduction. Material Removal Forming Processes. 2.2. Theoretical Foundations of Machining. 2.3. Conventional Machining Processes. 2.4. Cutting Tools. 2.5. Non-Conventional Machining Processes.

Block 3. Technologies and Material Conservation Forming Processes. 3.1. Introduction. Material Conservation Forming Processes. 3.2. Foundations and Technologies of Consolidation Forming Processes. 3.3. Foundations and Technologies of Plastic Deformation Forming Processes.
Block 4. Joining Technologies. 4.1. Introduction to joining technologies. 4.2 Welding Joining Processes. 4.3 Mechanical and chemical joining processes.

Block 5. Metrology. 5.1. Foundations of Metrology. Dimensional Metrology and quality. 5.2. Measurement of lengths and Angles 5.3 Measurement of Surface Finish and Geometry. 5.4 Quality Control in Manufacturing.
Block 6. Additive Manufacturing 6.1. Introduction to additive manufacturing processes. 6.2. Additive Manufacturing Processes.
Practice Blocks (2 sessions of 5 hours) Practice 1. Foundry and machining.
Practice 2. Additive manufacturing, Welding, plastic deformation and metrology.
teaching_methods: Workshop/laboratory practices in small working groups for consolidating theoretical knowledge.
Individual study and autonomous work (60 hours) for assimilating theoretical and practical content.
Group work (16 hours) for developing evaluation activities and solving proposed practical problems/exercises.
Tutoring sessions (individual or small groups) for resolving doubts and providing educational guidance.
Written exams for theoretical and practical parts of the subject (evaluation activity).
Theoretical classes, seminars, and expository lectures, including practical application examples and specialist conferences.
Practical classes/seminars for discussing and solving exercises and problems in small working groups, applying theoretical concepts, principles, and methodologies.

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical/practical exam (written exam based on problem-solving, short theoretical questions, multiple-choice questions, and/or essay questions)

Evaluable activities (developed throughout the semester after each thematic block, including numerical/conceptual problem-solving, element modeling, short synthesis reports, partial tests, and group project creation/presentation)
Practical exam (multiple-choice exam on practical content covered during laboratory practice sessions)
